# Planning Artifact Quality Checklist: Editor, File, Help, and Stream Components

**Purpose**: Validate the quality, completeness, consistency, and review readiness of `plan.md` and its associated planning artifacts before task generation or implementation.
**Created**: 2026-03-21
**Feature**: [plan.md](../plan.md), [research.md](../research.md), [data-model.md](../data-model.md), [public-api.md](../contracts/public-api.md), [quickstart.md](../quickstart.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and planning artifacts.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are all artifact roles explicitly defined so reviewers can tell why `plan.md`, `research.md`, `data-model.md`, `public-api.md`, and `quickstart.md` each exist and what decision surface each one owns? [Completeness, Plan §Planned Artifact Status]
- [x] CHK002 Are module responsibilities defined for every planned feature family so no editor, help, file, stream, or resource concern is left without an owning artifact or module boundary? [Completeness, Plan §Summary, Plan §Responsibility Boundaries]
- [x] CHK003 Are all clarified scope decisions from the feature specification reflected in at least one planning artifact, including dedicated help files, shared-reference preservation without cyclic graphs, case-sensitive resource keys, preserved line endings, `LF` defaults for new files, and explicit overwrite decisions? [Completeness, Plan §Summary, Research Decisions 3-9, Contract §Behavioral Guarantees]
- [x] CHK004 Does the data model define an entity or validation rule for every persistence-sensitive concept the plan depends on, including file snapshots, history buckets, help indexes, reference tables, and named resources? [Completeness, Data Model §Entities]
- [x] CHK005 Are explicit out-of-scope items documented consistently enough that reviewers can reject example-port, macro, calculator, OS-shell, or generalized windowing work as non-requirements for this increment? [Completeness, Plan §Summary, Plan §Customization Boundary for This Increment, Contract §Behavioral Guarantees]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK006 Is the term "single-interaction-cycle" clarified with enough precision that reviewers can distinguish an acceptable responsiveness requirement from an implied optimization request? [Clarity, Plan §Technical Context, Plan §Non-Functional Operationalization]
- [x] CHK007 Are the terms "explicit overwrite decision", "history bucket", "dedicated help file", and "supporting host frame" defined clearly enough that later tasks cannot reinterpret them in conflicting ways? [Clarity, Plan §Terminology & Operational Definitions]
- [x] CHK008 Is the difference between memory-only editing, file-backed editing, and file-dialog selection made explicit enough that responsibility boundaries are not left to inference? [Clarity, Contract §§`TMemo`, `TFileEditor`, `TFileDialog`, Data Model §§DocumentSession, FileAttachment, FileDialogSession]
- [x] CHK009 Are the plan's testing obligations described at the requirements level rather than as broad "cover everything" statements that leave scenario intent ambiguous? [Clarity, Plan §Testing Strategy, Contract §Test Obligations]
- [x] CHK010 Is the condition for widening scope toward a broader window abstraction stated clearly enough that implementers know when escalation is required instead of making a local design assumption? [Clarity, Plan §Dependencies & Assumptions, Plan §Risks & Mitigations]

## Requirement Consistency & Traceability

- [x] CHK011 Can each success criterion (`SC-001` to `SC-005`) be traced from the specification into a concrete planning hook without relying on implied coverage? [Traceability, Plan §Success-Criteria Traceability, Plan §Traceability Matrix]
- [x] CHK012 Are the dedicated-help-file requirements stated consistently across the research decisions, data model, API contract, and quickstart outcomes? [Consistency, Research Decision 4, Data Model §§HelpFileModel-HelpTopic, Contract §§`THelpFile`, `THelpViewer` and `THelpWindow`, Quickstart §Expected Outcomes]
- [x] CHK013 Are shared-reference preservation and cyclic-graph exclusion described consistently across the research decisions, data model, API contract, and quickstart outcomes? [Consistency, Research Decision 3, Data Model §StreamContext, Contract §§`pstream`, `ipstream`, `opstream`, `fpstream`, Quickstart §Expected Outcomes]
- [x] CHK014 Are case-sensitive resource-key semantics described consistently across the research decisions, data model, API contract, and quickstart outcomes? [Consistency, Research Decision 9, Data Model §§ResourceCatalog-ResourceEntry, Contract §`TResourceFile`, Quickstart §Expected Outcomes]
- [x] CHK015 Are line-ending preservation rules and external file-conflict handling aligned across the research decisions, data model, API contract, and quickstart outcomes? [Consistency, Research Decisions 6-7, Data Model §§DocumentSession-FileSnapshot, Contract §`TFileEditor`, Quickstart §Expected Outcomes]
- [x] CHK016 Are coverage-gate expectations for `TuiVision.Controls` and `TuiVision.Serialization` stated consistently with the rest of the repository guidance, or is any deliberate extension of the governance rule called out explicitly? [Consistency, Plan §Technical Context, Plan §Testing Strategy, Plan §Dependencies & Assumptions, Assumption]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK017 Are reviewer-readiness criteria specific enough to fail planning review when an artifact omits editor state, file-dialog synchronization, help navigation, or stream/resource semantics? [Measurability, Plan §Reviewer Readiness Criteria]
- [x] CHK018 Are the planned validation commands and conditional doc-generation step described precisely enough that reviewers can distinguish mandatory quality gates from optional follow-up work? [Measurability, Plan §Testing Strategy, Quickstart §§Planned Validation Flow-Expected Outcomes]
- [x] CHK019 Do the API behavioral guarantees describe observable outcomes rather than internal implementation choices, so later task breakdown can remain flexible without losing acceptance meaning? [Acceptance Criteria Quality, Contract §Behavioral Guarantees]
- [x] CHK020 Is the quickstart outcome section specific enough that each planned workflow has an objectively reviewable result rather than a general intent statement? [Measurability, Quickstart §Expected Outcomes]

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK021 Are primary, alternate, exception, recovery, and non-functional scenario classes all represented across the scenario matrix and state-transition sections, or are any of these scenario classes missing without an explicit exclusion? [Coverage, Plan §Scenario Matrix, Data Model §State Transitions, Gap]
- [x] CHK022 Are close-with-unsaved-changes requirements distinguished clearly from overwrite-conflict requirements so document-discard decisions and save-conflict decisions cannot be conflated later? [Coverage, Plan §Summary, Data Model §Document Session Lifecycle, Gap]
- [x] CHK023 Are file-dialog requirements complete enough for browsing, empty-result states, manual path entry, wildcard filtering, and history recall to be reviewed as one coherent scenario family? [Coverage, Plan §Scenario Matrix, Data Model §FileDialogSession]
- [x] CHK024 Are help requirements complete enough for valid context lookup, missing-context fallback, and zero-cross-reference topics without leaving any of those runtime cases implied? [Coverage, Plan §Scenario Matrix, Data Model §§HelpFileModel-CrossReference]
- [x] CHK025 Are malformed-input scenarios sufficiently enumerated so truncated data, trailing data, unknown types, and unsupported cycles are all explicitly covered by requirements rather than assumed under "invalid input"? [Coverage, Data Model §Stream Read Lifecycle, Plan §Testing Strategy]

## Non-Functional Requirements & Assumptions

- [x] CHK026 Are cross-platform file-system assumptions documented precisely enough that path handling, temp-file usage, and metadata-based conflict detection are reviewable as requirements rather than hidden implementation details? [Dependencies, Plan §Technical Context, Plan §Dependencies & Assumptions]
- [x] CHK027 Are documentation obligations for bilingual XML comments and docfx regeneration attached clearly enough to the planned public API changes that they cannot be deferred accidentally? [Completeness, Plan §Constitution Check, Plan §Testing Strategy, Contract §Test Obligations]
- [x] CHK028 Are the assumptions about a new `tests/TuiVision.Serialization.Tests` project explicit enough that reviewers can confirm the added test-surface expectation before task generation? [Dependencies, Research Decision 10, Plan §Project Structure, Plan §Dependencies & Assumptions]
- [x] CHK029 Are non-functional requirements intentionally bounded so observability, security hardening, and formal performance targets are clearly deferred rather than silently missing? [Boundaries, Plan §Non-Functional Operationalization, Plan §Dependencies & Assumptions, Gap]
- [x] CHK030 Are the identified risks paired with requirement-level mitigations that are specific enough to guide later task decomposition without dictating premature implementation details? [Consistency, Plan §Risks & Mitigations]

## Notes

- Durchfuehrungshinweis: Diese Checkliste ist fuer einen Dokumenten-Review vor `/speckit.tasks` gedacht, nicht fuer Code- oder Laufzeitverifikation.
- Durchfuehrungshinweis: Jede Frage ist gegen die geschriebenen Anforderungen in `plan.md` und den zugehoerigen Artefakten zu beantworten; fehlende oder nur implizite Aussagen gelten als offener Punkt.
- Durchfuehrungshinweis: Offene Punkte sollten inline mit kurzer Fundstelle oder mit `[Gap]`, `[Ambiguity]`, `[Conflict]` oder `[Assumption]` kommentiert werden.
- Durchfuehrungshinweis: Erst wenn kritische Punkte aus dieser Checkliste geklaert sind, sollte die Aufgabenzerlegung in `tasks.md` finalisiert werden.
- Review abgeschlossen am 2026-03-21 nach gezielten Klarstellungen in `plan.md`, `data-model.md`, `contracts/public-api.md` und `quickstart.md`.
